text:
zoe: quick heads-up — finished a boundary-scan across RoPE variants (linear / NTK / YARN) for Llama-70b and Mixtral-8x at ctx=8k/16k/32k. Observed unstable kernel-handoff behavior when YARN scaling crosses ~16k; switches are frequent and we see KV thrash. attaching a small dump below.

mike: can you paste the perf numbers you saw? rough latency and switch counts?

zoe: sure, pasted raw profiler snippets below (nvprof trimmed):
```
model=llama-70b, variant=YARN, ctx=16k
- avg_token_latency: 44.7ms
- kernel_switch_rate: 7.9 switches/s
- kv-cache-evictions: 12/min under steady load
- cpu-offload spikes when switch happens

model=llama-70b, variant=YARN, ctx=32k
- avg_token_latency: 71.3ms
- kernel_switch_rate: 12.4 switches/s
- kv-cache-evictions: 28/min

model=mixtral-8x, variant=NTK, ctx=16k
- avg_token_latency: 38.2ms
- kernel_switch_rate: 0.6 switches/s
- kv-cache-evictions: 1/min
```

anita: interesting — so NTK stays stable while YARN flips. Did you correlate to batch size distribution? Could batching heuristics be stepping on kernel selection heuristics?

zoe: yes, the flip windows line up with a shift in effective batch occupancy (many requests with long prefixes cause runtime to switch to long-kernel, then small bursts reverse it). kernel selector currently uses a cost-delta threshold of 15% and a 3-token hysteresis. that short hysteresis lets it oscillate for mixed-length workloads.

sam: how bad is quality impact? any perplexity/regression when the kernel flips mid-request?

zoe: we measure small but visible quality regressions on Mistral/YARN at long ctx. Using an eval prompt set:
- mistral-yarn ctx=12k: baseline ppl=15.2, with oscillation ppl=15.8 (+3.9%)
- mistral-ntk ctx=12k: baseline ppl=15.1, with oscillation ppl=15.2 (+0.7%)
So YARN oscillation correlates with 3-5% ppl spikes (mostly around early kv eviction points).

mike: hypothesis: two interacting systems — batching heuristics that try to maximize throughput and kernel selector that assumes stable seq-len distribution. When a 'heavy' request is batched with lots of small ones, the selector toggles, triggering kernel recompile/selection and causing KV eviction or memory pressure + padding changes. The cost model underestimates the switching overhead.

zoe: exactly. also saw that when head_kv_dim mismatch is present (some Mixtral configs with reused kv layout), the eviction cost is higher; kernel handoff ends up forcing a full KV normalize which spikes both latency and token loss window.

infra-bot: perf-run finished. artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1769123456/ (profiles + heap traces)

anita: what's our immediate mitigation? increasing hysteresis seems low-risk. also we could clamp batch formation when any request's kv-mem > 80% of model slot.

mike: proposed quick experiment set:
1) increase kernel selector hysteresis tokens from 3 -> 12
2) increase cost-delta threshold from 15% -> 30% for YARN variants
3) add batch-clamp rule: if any request predicts KV occupancy > 80%, put it in a separate batch (or route to pinned kernel)
4) pin kernel for models with head_kv mismatch until we can realign layout in compile-time

zoe: ran the hysteresis-only test locally:
- YARN ctx=16k after change: avg_token_latency dropped 44.7 -> 41.9ms, kernel_switch_rate 7.9 -> 1.1 switches/s, kv-evictions 12/min -> 2/min. ppl regression reduced from +3.9% -> +1.0%.

sam: sweet. can we canary this in staging with a control group? we should A/B against current config and gather latency, switch-rate, and ppl on the eval set.

anita: i'll add the eval harness and a focused prompt set targeting kv-edge cases (repeats, long-range coreference, padding-heavy).

mike: i'll wire a runtime flag so we can flip hystersis without deploy. call it `runtime.kernel_hysteresis_tokens` with per-model override.

zoe: plan for next 72h:
- mike: implement flag + canary (A/B traffic split)
- anita: add eval set and automated PPL check into canary metrics
- sam: schedule canary run and watch infra dashboard for memory churn

sam: noted — scheduling for tomorrow ~10:30 PDT. tagging infra to watch artifacts.

zoe: final note — long-term we should revisit kernel selection cost model to add explicit eviction / KV-rebuild penalty, and to incorporate batch composition heuristics into the selector input. this will avoid ad-hoc hysteresis tuning per-model.

mike: +1. let's file a short RFC and mark `kernel-selection` as owner.

zoe: assigning: @mike to run A/B and PR the runtime flag, @anita to add eval set and script, @sam to own canary run. :thumbsup:
